rule:
Except for spiral staircases, an intermediate landing must be provided at intervals of not more than 18 risers: no stair flight may rise more than 18 risers without a landing.

Regulatory text (the authoritative clauses - use them to interpret the requirement and its applicability; you must still work out how to read or measure it from the IFC):
BCA Approved Document (Acceptable Solutions) V7.08 - applicability:
E.2.1 A staircase (including a flight of 2 steps or more) shall provide a safe and suitable passage for movement of people.
E.2.2 A staircase must have - ... (b) landings to break a fall and provide a place for rest; (c) sufficient width, tread and riser to avoid injury; ...
E.2.4 The requirements in paragraph E.2.2(b) and (c) do not apply to a staircase located in any of the following rooms or spaces:
  (a) any equipment or plant room;
  (b) any production area of an industrial building;
  (c) any attic that - (ii) does not exceed an area of 10 square metres; and (iii) is in a residential building;
  (d) any house built for the owner's own use.
E.3.5 Landing:
E.3.5.1 A landing shall be provided at every floor level and door opening.
E.3.5.2 Except for spiral staircases, an intermediate landing shall be provided in between floor levels at intervals of not more than 18 risers.
E.3.5.4 ... A winder does not constitute a landing ... (winders are counted as risers).

Label every stair flight. A flight is one run between landings or floor levels; its riser count includes the final riser up to the landing or floor it arrives at. Label a flight NA when it belongs to a spiral staircase or to a staircase exempt under E.2.1 or E.2.4. Building use is not recorded in these models: a space named as a production area is treated as a production area of an industrial building (E.2.4(b)). A flight whose riser count cannot be determined cannot be judged: label it ALERT, and do NOT report it as a violation.
Report the GlobalId of every element (modelled as IfcStairFlight) that does NOT satisfy this requirement.

reference.status: IFC evidence: recorded riser counts corroborated by step geometry; applicability from building properties and containing spaces. Not expert certification.
reference.policy: Riser count per flight includes the arrival riser. A recorded count equal on every flight of a multi-flight stair and equal to the sum of their geometric counts is treated as the staircase total. Spiral staircase flights and E.2.1/E.2.4-exempt staircases are NA.
reference.limitations: Building use is not recorded in every model; E.2.4 relies on space names/occupancy and building properties. Geometric counts come from tread-face levels.
